_source: Our own table: docs/eras/luv.md, "Sunlight: one authoritative table" (decision 9 of 2026-10-25). The as-built rows repeat the values the EV and IV machines were built with (startup_scripts/grindless/ev/lunar_power_and_antenna.js, iv/mercury.js); tools/analysis/test/luv-foundation.test.mjs keeps them equal.
_how_it_is_used: startup_scripts/grindless/luv/foundation.js loads it into global.grindless.tables.sunlight; G.sunlight.factor(dimension) gives a dimension's factor, or null where no solar machine works or the dimension is not listed. Every solar machine from LuV on reads it.
factor: sunlight against Earth's surface by day under a clear sky (1.0). A lit panel of the solar family gives 300 EU/t times its factor (the lunar array's base), times the machine's own cell bonus.
rule (new airless places): the Moon's 1.4 at 1 AU divided by the square of the distance in AU. As-built values stay as built.

when: day = only while the place is lit (GTM's daytime check where the place has a day cycle), always = sky exposure only (orbits are always midnight, fixed_time 18000, so no orbital machine uses a daytime condition), never = no solar machine.

status: reference, as_built (era), new (LuV), no_solar. The LuV places' ids (grindless:asteroid_belt, io, europa, ganymede) are the design's proposals and are final only after spike S0-1; this table does not register them.
Any other orbit: its planet's factor by the rule, always (for later stations); add its row when the station is built.

minecraft:overworld.note: the family's reference: Earth's surface by day, clear sky

gcyr:venus.note: no solar machine: Venus has the heat engine

grindless:saturn_orbit.note: sky exposure only; the row exists to stop accidental solar builds (docs/eras/zpm.md)

grindless:uranus_orbit.note: sky exposure only; the row exists to stop accidental solar builds (docs/eras/zpm.md)

grindless:neptune_orbit.note: 1.4 / 30.1^2; sky exposure only; the row exists to stop accidental solar builds (docs/eras/uv.md)

grindless:pluto_orbit.note: 1.4 / 39.5^2; sky exposure only; the row exists to stop accidental solar builds (docs/eras/uv.md)

gcyr:mercury_orbit.note: 1.4 / 0.387^2; sky exposure only; the swarm's segments are rated here (docs/eras/uhv.md)

grindless:proxima_b_orbit.note: 65 % of Earth orbit (1.4 x 0.65), mostly near-infrared; distanceAU is the Sun-equivalent distance (Proxima b is 0.049 AU from a far dimmer star); sky exposure only

gcyr:proxima_centauri_b.note: the day side, as the orbit (65 % of Earth orbit): GCYR fixes Proxima b's time at 18000 (tidally locked), so 'day' is its star-side biome gcyr:proxima_centauri_b_star_side (GTM's biome condition), 0 elsewhere; the lunar solar field's Proxima row (273 EU/t per panel, x0.65 of the Moon's 420); Sun-equivalent distance as the orbit

grindless:alpha_centauri_orbit.note: Alpha Centauri A (G2V, 1.52 Lsun) at about 1.2 AU; IMM arrays at full yield; sky exposure only (docs/eras/uev.md)

grindless:barnard_b.note: M4V far-red light: 6.7 = 1.4 / 0.457^2 (Sun-equivalent distance, as Proxima's; Barnard b itself is 0.023 AU from a dim star); red-tuned arrays only (UHV's Proxima rule, x0.65); day side only

grindless:sirius_b_orbit.note: 5.6 = 1.4 / 0.5^2 (Sun-equivalent distance; Sirius B is 25,000 K hard UV): arrays degrade, no solar row; sky exposure only

grindless:rx_j1856_orbit.note: UIV-B1: soft X-ray, thermal (a cooling neutron star at 700,000 K); no solar machine; sky exposure only

grindless:psr_j0437_orbit.note: UIV-B1: pulsed X-ray and radio from a millisecond pulsar; no solar machine; sky exposure only

grindless:cygnus_x1_orbit.note: UIV-B1: 0.6 = 1.4 / 1.53^2 (Sun-equivalent distance); O-supergiant UV and the accretion disc's X-rays, a weak, hard light; sky exposure only

grindless:vela_pulsar_orbit.note: UXV-B1: the Vela pulsar's pulsed X-rays and radio; no solar machine; sky exposure only

grindless:cas_a_remnant.note: UXV-B1: Cassiopeia A's expanding supernova shell and its neutron star; no solar machine; sky exposure only

grindless:sgr1806_orbit.note: OpV-F1: a magnetar's X-ray and gamma bursts behind the bulge's dust; no solar machine; sky exposure only

grindless:terzan5_core.note: OpV-F1: the cluster core's dense, dust-reddened starlight and its millisecond pulsars; no solar machine; sky exposure only

gcyr:black_hole_orbit.note: MAX-F2: an accretion disc's hard X-rays; no solar machine; sky exposure only

grindless:nsc_belt.note: MAX-F2: the nuclear star cluster's crowded, dust-reddened stars; no solar machine; sky exposure only
